screening_decisions.reason: Double-blind RCT comparing carbamazepine vs diphenylhydantoin (phenytoin) monotherapy in 38 patients with psychomotor (focal) epilepsy. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, compares carbamazepine and phenytoin as monotherapy, appropriate seizure type (focal/psychomotor epilepsy).

While this is an RCT comparing phenytoin and carbamazepine monotherapy, the primary outcome is cognitive function (neuropsychological testing), not the review's target outcomes of time to treatment failure, remission, or first seizure. Does not address the review objective.
This is a systematic review/meta-analysis synthesizing data from 20 RCTs, not a primary randomized controlled trial. The selection criteria require primary RCTs only.

Prospective RCT comparing four antiepileptic drugs including carbamazepine and phenytoin as monotherapy in 243 adults with tonic-clonic or partial seizures. Outcomes include time to first seizure and time to remission. Meets all selection criteria.
Methodological paper discussing principles of equivalence trial design. Not a clinical trial comparing carbamazepine and phenytoin.
Prospective observational cohort study of 525 patients with newly diagnosed epilepsy. Not a randomized controlled trial comparing specific drugs. Does not meet study design criteria.
Review article discussing principles of AED therapy. Not a primary clinical trial. Does not meet study design criteria.

Non-randomized study examining cognitive function outcomes. While it includes patients on carbamazepine and phenytoin, it is not an RCT and does not assess seizure-related outcomes (treatment failure, remission, first seizure).
Animal study (rats) examining phenytoin-folate interactions. Not a human clinical trial. Does not meet population or study design criteria.

Prospective RCT comparing four antiepileptic drugs including carbamazepine and phenytoin as monotherapy in 167 children with tonic-clonic or partial seizures. Outcomes include time to first seizure and time to 1-year remission. Meets all selection criteria.
Epidemiological study estimating prevalence/incidence of neurologic disorders. Not a clinical trial comparing treatments. Does not meet study design criteria.

Study evaluates carbamazepine in patients whose seizures were NOT controlled by combination therapy (not newly diagnosed monotherapy candidates). Also, while it mentions comparison to phenobarbital/diphenylhydantoin, it does not appear to be a direct RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin monotherapy in the target population.
Epidemiological study of epilepsy incidence in HMO populations. Not a clinical trial comparing treatments. Does not meet study design criteria.

10-center double-blind RCT comparing four antiepileptic drugs including carbamazepine and phenytoin as monotherapy in 622 adults with partial and secondarily generalized tonic-clonic seizures. Follow-up for 2 years or until treatment failure. Meets all selection criteria.
Review article discussing diagnostic accuracy and case ascertainment in epilepsy epidemiology. Not a clinical trial. Does not meet study design criteria.

Non-randomized study examining somatosensory evoked potentials (neurophysiological measure), not seizure-related outcomes. While it compares phenytoin and carbamazepine monotherapy, it does not assess treatment failure, remission, or first seizure. Does not meet outcome criteria.
Population-based incidence study of epilepsy in Iceland. Not a clinical trial comparing treatments. Does not meet study design criteria.
Methodological paper describing statistical methods for meta-analysis. Uses epilepsy trials only as illustrations. Not a primary clinical trial. Does not meet study design criteria.
Meta-analysis estimating global burden/prevalence of epilepsy. Not a primary clinical trial comparing carbamazepine and phenytoin. Does not meet study design criteria.
Position paper updating epilepsy classification terminology. Not a clinical trial. Does not meet study design criteria.
Double-blind RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin (diphenylhydantoin) as monotherapy in patients with temporal lobe epilepsy (focal onset seizures). Meets all selection criteria.
Review article about dermatological uses of phenytoin, not a clinical trial comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin for epilepsy treatment.
Double-blind crossover RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin as monotherapy in 47 patients with focal and major generalized seizures. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT randomly assigning 64 children with epilepsy to carbamazepine, phenytoin, or valproate monotherapy. Contains direct comparison of carbamazepine vs phenytoin as monotherapy in children with epilepsy.
In vitro mechanistic study on GABA receptor modulation in cell cultures, not a clinical trial in humans.
Study focused on zonisamide pharmacokinetics and drug interactions, not a comparison of carbamazepine vs phenytoin monotherapy.
In vitro electrophysiological study on mouse neuroblastoma cells, not a clinical trial in humans.
Methodological guideline document for systematic reviews, not a primary clinical trial.
Multi-arm trial comparing phenobarbital, mephobarbital, primidone, diphenylhydantoin, ethotoin, metharbital, and methylphenylhydantoin - does not include carbamazepine as a comparator.
Network meta-analysis of individual participant data, not a primary RCT. This is a secondary synthesis study.
Observational case series of 15 children with seizure exacerbation on carbamazepine, not a randomized controlled trial comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin.
Cochrane systematic review on congenital malformations, not a primary RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin.
Small case series of 5 children with aberrant reactions to carbamazepine, not a randomized controlled trial.
Double-blind crossover RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin as sole treatment (monotherapy) in 45 patients with partial and generalized epilepsy. Meets all selection criteria.
Clinical Q&A article/editorial about carbamazepine safety in pregnancy, not a primary clinical trial.
Prospective RCT randomly assigning 55 patients with epilepsy to carbamazepine, phenytoin, or phenobarbitone monotherapy. Contains direct comparison of carbamazepine vs phenytoin as monotherapy.
Observational cross-sectional study measuring serum zinc and copper levels in patients already on monotherapy, not a randomized controlled trial.
Controlled double-blind trial of carbamazepine. Abstract does not clearly specify the comparator drug - may include phenytoin comparison. Including conservatively for full-text review.
Prospective trials comparing phenytoin and carbamazepine monotherapy in newly diagnosed patients with grand mal or partial seizures. Design details unclear from abstract - including conservatively.
Prospective controlled observational study on congenital malformations in children exposed in utero to phenytoin or carbamazepine, not a randomized controlled trial.

This is a double-blind crossover RCT comparing carbamazepine (CBZ) with diphenylhydantoin/phenytoin (DPH) in epileptic patients. The study reports seizure outcomes and side effects for both drugs, meeting the selection criteria for a RCT comparing CBZ vs phenytoin monotherapy.

This is a Cochrane review about prenatal exposure to AEDs and neurodevelopmental outcomes in children. It does not report a primary RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin monotherapy for seizure control.
This is a methodological paper discussing IPD meta-analysis approaches in AED research. It is not a primary RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin.
This is an observational registry study about congenital malformations in pregnancy. It is not a RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin monotherapy for seizure control.
This is a methodological paper about meta-analysis statistics (I² statistic). It is not a clinical trial.
This is a methodological paper about outcome reporting bias in systematic reviews. It is not a primary RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin.
This is an epidemiological incidence study of epilepsy. It is not a RCT comparing treatments.
This is a case series of 4 adults describing absence seizures associated with carbamazepine therapy. It is not a RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin.
This is an in vitro preclinical study examining drug effects on Na+ channels in mammalian cells. It is not a clinical RCT in humans.
This is an observational epidemiological study describing the natural history of epilepsy. It is not a RCT comparing treatments.

This is a counterbalanced, double-blind crossover RCT comparing carbamazepine with phenytoin in 40 adult epileptics. While the primary focus is psychotropic/cognitive effects, it is a valid RCT comparing the two drugs of interest in patients with epilepsy.
This is a Cochrane review comparing phenobarbitone vs phenytoin. It does not involve carbamazepine, which is required by the selection criteria.
This is an observational record linkage study about cutaneous reactions. It is not a RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin monotherapy for seizure control.
This is a prospective cohort study about prognostic factors for epilepsy remission. It is not a RCT comparing treatments.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing phenytoin (DPH) and carbamazepine (CBZ) in 40 newly diagnosed, drug-naive adult epileptic patients. Patients were randomized into DPH and CBZ groups, meeting the selection criteria for a RCT comparing these two drugs.
This is a RCT comparing phenobarbital vs phenytoin in children. While it involves phenytoin, it does not include carbamazepine, which is required by the selection criteria.
This is a methodological paper about extracting statistics for meta-analysis. It is not a clinical trial.
